patch.value:
## The seam

pm-klxax7 names this the programme's binding prerequisite: an episode spans several pm invocations, some through the CLI and some through MCP, and there is no key that identifies the episode across them. Without that key, trajectory projection (pm-qd6gvf) cannot group observation-action-outcome sequences, fleet attribution (pm-gw6uyq) cannot aggregate per-run, and the episode substrate (pm-li2fj5) has a unit with no identity.

The epic owns the seam. This item is the closeable tranche that delivers it.

## What exists today, measured

Every history entry carries `agent_instance`, a per-session identifier assigned by harness detection. On a live claude-code session a mutation records:

```
author            harness:claude-code
author_source     detected
agent_harness     claude-code
agent_instance    34ce3d428d5811b4f30f6318
agent_provenance  { model: null, effort: { value: xhigh, source: environment }, role: null }
```

`agent_instance` is the closest thing to an episode key that exists, and it is not one, for three separate reasons.

It is a harness-session identity, not a task identity. One agent session that works three unrelated items produces one instance value spanning all three; three sessions that collaborate on one item produce three. Episodes and sessions are different partitions of the same event stream, and the substrate currently only records the second.

It is surface-dependent. pm-1zhfls established that the MCP server does not receive the harness provenance environment, so the same agent session records different provenance depending on whether a mutation went through the CLI or through a tool call. An episode that mixes both is recorded as two.

It is unlabelled. pm-rbg1qo established that no role or session topic has ever been recorded on any harness. Nothing in the record says what the episode was *for*, so grouping by instance yields anonymous partitions that a training or evaluation run cannot select on.

## What the key has to be

A first-class recorded dimension, not a derived heuristic. Co-mutation cohort inference (a pm-4k6b catalog entry) reconstructs plausible working sessions from mutation timing, and that is the right technique when nothing was declared — but an environment author knows the episode boundary exactly, and inferring what is known is a needless loss of precision. Both must exist: the declared key when present, the inference when absent.

Stable across process, surface, and harness. The same episode observed from a CLI invocation, an MCP tool call, and a direct SDK call must record the same key, which means the key propagates through the same channel discipline pm-ffz0a9 establishes for provenance rather than through a fourth ad-hoc mechanism.

Labelled. An episode carries a declared purpose — role, topic, or task descriptor — because an unlabelled partition is not selectable, and selection is the entire point of recording it.

Nestable. A delegated sub-agent is a sub-episode of its parent; the environment `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` already distinguishes this in the environment today. A flat key cannot express a fleet where agents spawn agents, and a fleet where agents spawn agents is the target.

Never load-bearing for correctness. A missing episode key degrades grouping; it must never fail a mutation, block a write, or change what is stored about the item itself.

## Acceptance shape

The falsifier is a single episode that deliberately crosses every boundary: begun through the SDK, continued through two CLI invocations, continued through an MCP tool call, delegated to a sub-episode that mutates a different item, and ended. Projecting trajectories over the resulting history must return exactly one episode with one nested child, and grouping by the key must be byte-identical whether the projection reads the streams in file order or in timestamp order.

The degenerate case is equally binding: a workspace where no episode is ever declared must record exactly what it records today, with the inference path supplying grouping and marking it as inferred rather than declared.

## Boundaries

Not provenance channel design (pm-ffz0a9), which owns how a dimension is observed. This owns which dimension exists and what it identifies.

Not dimension coverage per harness (pm-rbg1qo), which owns whether role and topic keys are declared for a given harness. This owns the episode as a unit, and consumes those keys as its label.

Not trajectory projection (pm-qd6gvf) or the episode substrate (pm-li2fj5), both of which consume this key and neither of which can define it without duplicating the other.
Episode identity: a stable, labelled, nestable episode key that survives process, surface and harness boundaries so trajectory grouping and fleet aggregation have a join key

First of the four seams pm-klxax7 owns, and the one it names its binding prerequisite. An episode spans several pm invocations across CLI, MCP and SDK surfaces, and the only per-session key recorded today is agent_instance, which is a harness-session identity rather than a task identity, is surface-dependent (pm-1zhfls: the MCP server does not receive the harness provenance environment, so one session records two identities), and is unlabelled (pm-rbg1qo: no role or topic has ever been recorded on any harness). Without a stable labelled key, pm-qd6gvf cannot group observation-action-outcome sequences and pm-gw6uyq cannot aggregate per run. Duplicate check: searched episode/session/trajectory/identity lineages, read pm-1zhfls (closed), pm-rbg1qo, pm-ffz0a9, pm-9wbiye, pm-li2fj5, pm-qd6gvf; the epic names this seam and no item owns it.

A declared episode key propagates unchanged across SDK, CLI and MCP invocations in one session; sub-episodes nest under their parent; each episode carries a declared label (role or topic); grouping trajectories by the key over a deliberately boundary-crossing episode returns exactly one episode with one nested child, order-independently; a workspace that never declares an episode records exactly what it records today and grouping falls back to the co-mutation inference marked as inferred; a missing key never fails, blocks or alters a mutation
Give the agent-environment programme a join key that identifies an episode rather than a harness session
Trajectory projection, fleet attribution and episode substrate all become groupable from the immutable record alone
pm-klxax7 names this the programme's binding prerequisite and three filed features consume it without any of them being able to define it
